newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - March 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - March 18.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

The National Heritage Select Committee has called for an end to self regulation and the adoption of a style similar to Channel 4's system in "The BBC and The Future of Broadcasting" report. They also call for an external watchdog to regulate taste and decency issues.
BIG GUNS BLAST GGT 8MN STG TAKEOVER FEES

Institutional investors in advertising group GGT are concerned that advisers are charging over 8 percent in its dealings involving the acquisition of French media firm BDDP. The deal is being funded by a 55 million stg placing and open offer and debt finance.
The pound fell yesterday due to pre-election jitters, the strength of the mark and the recent fall in UK interest rates.
Analysts are expecting weak VAT receipts for March.
NUMBERS GAME ADDS SPICE TO A 'LABOUR VICTORY'

Dave Brown of William Hill said the Conservatives are 8-1 against winning the general election outright. Most money is being bet on how many seats the Labour Party will win and who will succeed John Major in the event of a Conservative defeat. William Hague is now joint favourite with Michael Portillo as the likely candidate.
